item.title: Bird Watching: Characterizing the Infrastructure and Behavior of Falcon-branded Extortion Operations
item.description:
UNC6671 / CORDIAL SPIDER runs a vishing-driven AitM operation under Falcon, Helix, Pink and Redact brands, hitting 76 organizations across financial services and legal sectors since April 2026, with $8M in confirmed extortion payments.
- The Work Panel platform is a full cybercrime-as-a-service console with role-based access (caller, manager, admin), automated target recon via RocketReach API, NICENIC domain provisioning, and real-time AitM credential relay. Callers never see captured creds. Three panel deployments identified: betterdays2828199[.]com, panel.sqfepjvmrd[.]xyz on 31.7.56[.]61, and panel.whatarewedoingwiththesedomainshello[.]com on 31.7.56[.]52, all on AS51852 (Private Layer INC).
- Post-auth pivot is the forensic chokepoint: once actors capture an Okta OTP via AitM, they authenticate and ride the OAuth token into M365, Salesforce, and connected SaaS. Evasion includes real-time deletion of concurrent security warning emails to the victim. Extortion arrives via TOX with a deadline after exfiltration completes.
- Kit fingerprints are durable across domain rotation. Hunt for api_FyekIDWY.php in HTTP requests, ETag W/"1c-xHTlhvqhxGIJKu5AJR5p+il839Y" in responses, and static asset d15faff9a15a05e605bc9cfadacdfb4f16ff2c9d.svg. Response hashes c51eb785... (Okta) and 275a824c... (M365) confirm the same kit build across all 118 URLScan hits.

item.title: Shattering the Dream – When a Job Offer Becomes a Zero-Day Attack
item.description:
Lazarus Operation Dream Job returns with a CVE-2026-68820 zero-day in AFD.sys, a new Troy backdoor, and RelayShell webshells turning compromised Roundcube servers into C2 relays targeting global defense.
- CVE-2026-68820 (patched August 11 Patch Tuesday, today) is a use-after-free race condition in afd.sys targeting Windows 11 builds 26100/26200. FudModule v3.1 exploits it via MISTPEN's LPE loader, negotiating keys with Kyber/ML-KEM before fetching the payload, achieving SYSTEM and blinding EDR. Hunt for Afd4Eop12_x64.dll and the string "enable_god_mode passed" on disk and in memory.
- Two parallel infection chains: Chain 1 uses DLL sideloading via libmupdf.dll to execute MISTPEN, which pulls modules (GetInfoPlugin, PvPlugin, OneScreenCapture64.dll) reflectively via Microsoft Graph API over OneDrive. Chain 2 uses SecurityPDF.exe, a trojanized MuPDF viewer that XOR-decrypts (key 0x39) payloads marked "This document is encrypted with sumatrapdf reader" and drops %TEMP%\new.exe loading the Troy backdoor.
- Troy is a 17-command modular RAT (PDB: Troy_Handle) communicating over HTTP to three C2s, supporting reflective DLL injection, WMI process enumeration, ZIP exfil via PowerShell Compress-Archive, and in-memory code delivery. C2 domains: envell[.]xyz, enveil[.]online, uxtramine[.]org. IPs: 135.181.67[.]203, 135.181.185[.]158.

item.title: Threat Hunting Case Study: The Gentlemen
item.description:
The Gentlemen ransomware group abuses privileged group manipulation and NETLOGON share staging to spread malware domain-wide before encryption begins. Hunt the technique early or face full-domain compromise.
- The group's attack chain pivots on adding accounts to privileged groups (T1098), then staging payloads in the NETLOGON share on Windows domain controllers so Group Policy pushes the malware to every joined endpoint automatically.
- The NETLOGON share (typically \\DC\NETLOGON) is a high-trust distribution path that most defenses under-monitor. Any file written there by a non-admin process or unexpected account is a critical signal worth immediate triage.
- Hunt for Event ID 4728 or 4732 (member added to privileged group) followed closely by file creation events under SYSVOL\domain\scripts or the NETLOGON path. That sequence, group change then share write, is the pre-encryption tell.
- Artifact focus: AD event logs on domain controllers, file system timestamps on NETLOGON, and Group Policy Object modification logs. Correlate with logon events (4624/4648) to identify the source account and lateral movement path.
Takeaway: Build a detection pairing Event ID 4728/4732 with NETLOGON write activity in your SIEM. A new file in that share from an unexpected principal should page someone immediately. Full hunt methodology and IOCs are in the Intel 471 report.

item.title: Gunra Ransomware Builds a New Attack Network Through RaaS
item.description:
Gunra ransomware, derived from leaked Conti source code, has formalized a RaaS affiliate program and drawn a joint FBI/CISA advisory. The group runs double-extortion operations across healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and government sectors globally.
- Initial access centers on two actively exploited FortiOS/FortiProxy authentication bypass flaws: CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472. Gunra actors also abused default VPN credentials where account lockout was absent, then leveraged stolen session tokens to pivot into internal VDI, Active Directory servers, and IT workstations via Impacket and SMB lateral movement.
- Data theft precedes encryption at scale. Actors used a malicious binary named main.exe to exfiltrate from Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint, then staged compressed archives to Mega. Exfiltrated volumes reached tens of terabytes before ChaCha20/RSA-4096 encryption deployed. Watch for .ENCRT and .CRYPT file extensions. WMI is used to delete volume shadow copies (T1490) and backup infrastructure was wiped across primary and DR sites.
- The affiliate program provides a management panel, configurable builder, and cross-platform payloads covering Windows and Linux. Gunra also operates under the alias Golden Community and recruits initial access brokers on dark web forums.
Prioritize patching CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 immediately. Hunt for main.exe, anomalous OneDrive/SharePoint API activity, and outbound transfers to Mega.

item.title: Bypassing Android Hardware Attestation from the Analyst's Chair
item.description:
Android hardware attestation relayed, not broken: Quarkslab shows how a Frida hook and a clean burner phone flip a backend verdict from rejected to valid without touching crypto or firmware.
Key findings:
- The attestation chain's RootOfTrust (tag [704] in hardwareEnforced) is what kills analysis on a rooted device. verifiedBootState reports Unverified and deviceLocked is false because those values are written by secure hardware before Android boots, no userspace patch changes them. The relay sidesteps this entirely by having a stock, locked phone generate the chain instead.
- The seam is KeystoreAttestation.generateAttestedKey(challenge: ByteArray). Frida hooks that single method, re-encodes the raw challenge bytes as unpadded base64url, ships it to the clean oracle device via HTTP POST /attest, and returns the resulting AttestedKey to the app. The local Keystore is never called. The app forwards a genuine chain it believes is its own.
- The backend cannot distinguish a relayed chain from a local one. KeyDescription carries no field binding the attestation to a transport session, network address, or process. The nonce (attestationChallenge) is the only freshness signal, and the relay forwards it untouched.
- The decisive mitigation is one backend comparison: read attestationApplicationId (tag [709], softwareEnforced) and reject any chain whose package name or signing certificate SHA-256 digest does not match the expected app.

item.title: Rapid7 Analysis: Microsoft SharePoint JWT Token Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-55040)
item.description:
CVE-2026-55040 is a critical auth bypass in SharePoint Server letting unauthenticated attackers forge JWT tokens and impersonate any user, including site admins, with a PoC now public.
- The root cause is a four-weakness chain in SPJsonWebSecurityTokenHandlerV2: RequireSignedTokens is explicitly set to false, accepting alg:none outer tokens with no crypto check; the actor token x5t thumbprint is resolved against SharePoint's own STS cert (retrievable unauthenticated from /_layouts/15/metadata/json/1) but never signature-verified; issuer validation silently accepts certs not in TrustedSecurityTokenServices; and GetTokenSignature only checks non-empty string, so "AAAA" passes as a valid RSA signature.
- Attack chain: fetch STS cert from /_layouts/15/metadata/json/1 unauthenticated, compute x5t, query domain controller via SMB null session on LSARPC to enumerate valid user SIDs, forge a nested JWT with alg:none outer header and a nameid SID targeting a domain admin, send Bearer token to any authenticated endpoint like /_api/web/currentuser and receive IsSiteAdmin:true.
- Affected version confirmed: SharePoint Server Subscription Edition 16.0.19725.20210. Rapid7 published a PoC on July 14, 2026 alongside disclosure. Patch immediately; with public PoC this is a trivially exploitable critical.

item.title: Head Mare APT is exploiting vulnerabilities in an unpatched TrueConf server to deliver PhantomCore and PhantomGraph to video conference participants
item.description:
Head Mare-targeting APT trojanized TrueConf video conference installers via two zero-day server vulns, dropping PhantomCore and PhantomGraph backdoors on victim endpoints.
- Head Mare chained KLCERT-26-057 and KLCERT-26-058 against TrueConf Server versions 5.3.x through 5.5.5 via unauthenticated port 4307/TCP. The first vuln allows remote script execution on the server; the second escapes the sandbox to reach NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. Once elevated, attackers replaced public/js/locale.php (MD5: 4d27b4eb1c5dbb3d8160f29b8119523e) with a web shell. Patches landed June 18, 2026 in versions 5.3.9, 5.4.9, and 5.5.5.
- The web shell gave access to the TrueConf database and swapped the legitimate client installer with a trojanized build (748c9f8cb1065000616204935f96207f) containing PhantomCore. Persistence lands via HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\{0340F119-A598-4ed9-B0AC-6F6A12D3E755}\InprocServer32. Critically, even organizations that do not run their own TrueConf server are at risk if employees connect to a partner's compromised instance.
- PhantomGraph (SysExcSvc.dll + SysReadSvc.dll installed as Windows services from %TEMP%) uses a Microsoft OneDrive account as C2, communicating via the Graph API. Commands execute through %TEMP%\cmd_cmd_*.bat batch files. Observed post-exploitation: lsass memory dumping via comsvcs.dll, SSH reverse tunnel creation, and reconnaissance via hostname/whoami. C2 IPs include 81.177.32[.]12 and 194.87.239[.]71.

item.title: Fake popular sites offer a free app, instead take over PCs
item.description:
Lookalike sites for CNN, Avast, and Stremio are silently installing O&O Syspectr, a legitimate signed RAT, pre-linked to attacker accounts. AV won't flag it because it is not malware.
Key findings:
- Attackers operate at least two Syspectr accounts. Account 4693fd-d903-4791-8f58-975261c93ca2 ties app.cnn-news[.]com, avast-premium[.]shop, and stremiotv[.]online together. Account 9158bf2a-ff25-4290-b96c-2dc5eb310391 runs syncminer[.]xyz and idleminer[.]pro. The account ID is embedded in the installer filename, making attribution straightforward once you have the file.
- The installers are genuine, digitally-signed software from O&O Software GmbH. Syspectr gives operators remote desktop, file browsing, command execution, and software installation at the admin level. Traditional AV has no basis to block a signed business tool, regardless of how it arrived.
- O&O responded within days: disabled Remote Desktop and Remote Console on free accounts, and suspended the abusive accounts. Their analysis confirmed attackers used Remote Console exclusively, not Remote Desktop.
Responder action: Hunt endpoints for Syspectr via installed programs or the process oo-syspectr-agent.exe. On any suspicious installer, right-click, Properties, Details tab: File description and Product name will show O&O Syspectr regardless of filename. If found without admin deployment, treat as full compromise, rotate credentials from a clean machine. Full IOC list in the report.

item.title: Project CAV3RN continues: Google Apps Script as C2 relay and DNS-based C2 channel selection
item.description:
Project CAV3RN, an espionage framework targeting Israel 🇮🇱, adds a DNS-driven C2 selector that switches between direct HTTPS and Google Apps Script relay per transaction, with operator-controlled channel rotation baked in.
- GoogleService.dll (MD5: 981c7404d31b8ce35ec88a6b290f354d), a .NET 8 NativeAOT DLL, queries a DNS A-record at <nonce><error-state>.<hex-client-ID>.m.studiotikva[.]com before every poll. The fourth octet of the response selects the channel: 120 = Google Apps Script or Direct HTTPS depending on error state, 130 = Direct HTTPS or close, 140 = exception. This means the operator can steer every individual C2 transaction at the DNS layer without touching the implant.
- The Google Apps Script relay is kept fresh via .q and .p DNS subdomains. A 32-bit MD5 prefix check validates the stored deployment ID; a mismatch triggers chunked retrieval over .p queries, delivering a new 74-character ID in 19 DNS responses. The recovered ID is written back to conf.json on disk, the only persistent update the module makes.
- The broker rnp.dll (MD5: 2dcd4a8ac166404977cd3c48418a8cd9) masquerades as the RNP OpenPGP library and hot-loads DLL components by scanning its host directory every second. Components must export GroupByCategory, CheckAvailability, IsPrimeNumber, and OrderByDate to be loaded. Payload XOR key is 0xAC; delimiter _;;_ separates commands from arguments.

item.title: Gunra ransomware expands globally as US, South Korean agencies warn of data theft, encryption and extortion tactics
item.description:
Gunra ransomware, a Conti-derived RaaS now operating globally, exploits FortiOS/FortiProxy auth bypasses and VPN default creds to hit healthcare, government, critical manufacturing and more across six regions.
Key findings:
- Initial access via CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 (auth bypass in FortiOS/FortiProxy) plus default credentials on SSL-VPN appliances. Lateral movement uses Impacket over SMB and stolen session tokens. Persistence achieved by installing OpenSSH and creating backdoor VPN accounts with password-change bypass.
- Credential theft via secretsdump.py against NTDS on domain controllers enabling pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket. Actors also modified VDI portal files to bypass MFA and stole symmetric encryption keys from a Hiware access control server via SSH.
- Gunra deletes logs and command history, operates 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., and uses IsDebuggerPresent to block analysis. The Windows encryptor uses FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW to traverse all drives A through Z with no network indicators.
- Critical decryption opportunity: Linux ELF variants as of March 2026 use a weak PRNG seeded with predictable system time. File timestamps can reconstruct encryption keys mathematically, making ransom payment unnecessary for Linux victims.
Patch CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 immediately. For Linux victims, preserve file timestamps and attempt key reconstruction before paying. Audit VPN accounts for password-change bypass and review NTDS access logs.

item.title: CopyEscape: Taking Over Docker Hosts with docker cp
item.description:
CVE-2026-17106: a container-to-host arbitrary file-write in docker cp lets a malicious container overwrite host files or achieve root code execution the moment a user runs a routine copy.
Key findings:
- The exploit chains two flaws in moby/go-archive v0.2.0: a TOCTOU race lets a live container swap a directory for an absolute symlink mid-walk, and the CLI extractor validates a constructed path but hands the raw symlink target to the kernel, writing outside the user-chosen destination. Validated on Docker Engine 29.6.1 and Docker Desktop 4.81.0.
- Impact splits by privilege: on macOS the write lands as the local user, enabling overwrite of shell startup scripts or ~/Library/LaunchAgents persistence. On Linux with sudo docker cp, the PoC replaced /usr/bin/runc with a shell script, converting a file write into root code execution on the next Docker lifecycle call.
- Also affects sbx cp in Docker Sandboxes: retrieving an artifact from an untrusted AI-agent sandbox triggers the same destination escape under CVE-2026-17106. Docker Sandboxes 0.38.0 (Aug 6) and Docker Desktop 4.86.0 with Engine 29.7.2 (Aug 10) ship the fixes.
- DFIR risk: copying evidence from a suspected compromised container can trigger a waiting payload. The copy that looked like safe data collection becomes the delivery mechanism.
Patch to Docker Engine/CLI 29.7.2 and Desktop 4.86.0 now. Until patched, stop the container before copying and avoid sudo docker cp.

item.title: Metabase Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild: Unauthenticated SQL Injection Leading to Full Admin Access
item.description:
GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf: CVSS 10.0, zero-day SQLi in Metabase's unauthenticated password reset endpoint gives attackers full admin takeover in a single HTTP request. Actively exploited in the wild before disclosure; Framework confirmed as a victim with customer PII exposed.
- The vulnerable sink is POST /api/session/reset_password, reachable without credentials by design. An attacker adds a user-id key as a HoneySQL {:raw "SQL"} object; no type validation occurs, so the value compiles into the WHERE clause, selects a superuser row, and the endpoint overwrites that admin's password with the attacker's value. One request, no auth, full admin.
- The IoC fingerprint Metabase published is precise: POST /api/session/reset_password returning HTTP 400 on a benign probe, immediately followed by the same endpoint returning HTTP 200, then GET /api/user/current returning 200 with is_superuser: true. Alert on that sequence in your web/proxy logs.
- Post-compromise scope is severe. Metabase stores credentials for every connected data source (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift). Admin access means those credentials are readable, enabling direct warehouse pivoting. Persistence paths include attacker-created API keys, new admin accounts, and wiped core_session rows.
- Affected: self-hosted v1.58 through v1.63, both OSS and EE, JAR or Docker. Fixed versions: v58.24, v59.21, v60.17, v61.11, v62.9, v63.5. Metabase Cloud was patched before disclosure.

item.title: Hunting Web Activity Before a Device Code Authentication (KQL Query)
item.description:
Device Code phishing hunts don't require a known-bad URL. This KQL technique pivots from the authentication event itself, reconstructing the three URLs visited in the five minutes before the Device Code flow to surface behavioural context no IOC feed can provide.
- Device Code phishing (T1528) abuses the OAuth device authorization flow to steal tokens without ever touching the user's credentials. IOC-based hunting works only after infrastructure is reported. This approach flips the model: anchor on the Cmsi:Cmsi event in EntraIdSignInEvents, then look backwards at DeviceNetworkEvents for the same AccountUpn over the preceding five minutes.
- The KQL builds a unique DeviceCodeId per authentication, joins it to network telemetry, uses partition with top 3 by WebTime to preserve only the three most recent URLs, and enriches each RemoteIP with a country via geo_info_from_ip_address. Output is three URL/country pairs per authentication event, ready to filter.
- Tuning is the payoff. Baseline out expected Microsoft endpoints (login.windows[.]net, mobile.events.data.microsoft[.]com) and known-good countries. What survives the allowlist, an unrecognised domain with zero TI reputation visited seconds before a Device Code auth from an unexpected country, is your lead regardless of whether any feed has ever seen that domain.
Pivot from the sequence, not the indicator.

item.title: Follow the File Hash: Hunting for Sensitive Files Leaving Your Organization with Defender Advanced…
item.description:
SHA256 as the pivot: correlating MDE endpoint telemetry, MDO email logs, and Purview IRM lets you trace a sensitivity-labeled file from the device where it lived to the Gmail inbox it landed in.
- DeviceFileEvents surfaces SensitivityLabel, SensitivitySubLabel, and SHA256 for every file-create, modify, rename, or delete event MDE observes. Filtering on isnotempty(SensitivityLabel) and excluding all-zero hashes gives you a live inventory of labeled files per device, including OneDrive-synced paths like C:\Users\...\OneDrive.
- EmailAttachmentInfo in MDO carries sender, recipient, filename, and SHA256 for every attachment. An inner join on SHA256 between the two tables bridges endpoint presence to outbound delivery, including recipient domain, without any DLP alert needing to fire first.
- The DataSecurityEvents table (Public Preview) in Purview IRM adds a third pivot: ActionType "email sent to free public domains" with parsed AttachmentInfo containing its own SHA256, enabling a second independent correlation path back to the endpoint file.
- The full three-way join is: DeviceFileEvents (file + label + hash) joined to DataSecurityEvents (Purview email + hash) to confirm a "General" or "Highly Confidential" labeled file reached Gmail, Yahoo, or Proton Mail, with sender UPN, subject line, and timestamp all in one result row.
Hunt tip: run the combined KQL against your tenant today scoped to high-value labels.

item.title: Mobile Forensics: Extracting Data from WhatsApp
item.description:
WhatsApp artifacts on Android and iOS mapped in detail: SQLite databases, encrypted backups, media trees, and shared prefs all hold evidence a mobile investigator needs to reconstruct communications.
Key findings:
- Android core evidence lives in /data/data/com.whatsapp/databases/: wa.db (contacts, phone numbers, display names) and msgstore.db (messages, timestamps, status, media references). Root or a physical image is required to read them directly. Encrypted backups at /data/media/0/WhatsApp/Databases/msgstore.db.cryptXX need the key from /data/data/com.whatsapp/files/ to decrypt.

item.title: A Deep Dive into LNK Files | Windows Forensics
item.description:
LNK files outlive deleted originals: Windows shortcut metadata records file interaction, source location, and device identity long after the target file disappears.
- LNK files are auto-created without user action when files are opened via File Explorer or Open/Save dialogs. Primary locations are C:\Users\<Username>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent and the Office equivalent under AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Office\Recent. They persist even after the original file is deleted, moved, or unplugged.
- Each LNK contains two distinct timestamp sets: source timestamps (the shortcut itself) and target timestamps (the original file). If target Created is newer than target Modified, the file was likely copied or moved, not originally created there. Conflating the two is a common analytical error.
- Volume serial number, volume label, drive type, UNC path, and machine name inside the LNK let you correlate removable-media access to USB registry artifacts without the drive being present. A LNK pointing to a removable drive cross-referenced with ShellBags and Jump Lists can identify the exact device and the folders browsed on it.
- Attackers weaponize LNK files by embedding PowerShell or other commands in the target path and command-line arguments fields, disguising malicious execution as a legitimate shortcut. Examine those fields during malware triage.

item.title: The security signal log tailing can't see: tracking npm cooldown removals with Elastic Agent
item.description:

item.description:

item.title: When Agentic Glue Melts: Exploiting Cloudflare Code Mode and Workers
item.description:
Five memory-corruption bugs in workerd, the runtime behind Cloudflare Workers and Code Mode, enable cross-tenant secret theft and sandbox escape to host RCE. Two rated Critical by Cloudflare. Patched in production; self-hosted deployments must update to v1.20260619.1.
Key findings:
- The attack surface is workerd's JSG layer, the C++ glue marshaling JavaScript calls into native code. Unlike V8, JSG had almost no prior public scrutiny, and the objects it allocates land on the tcmalloc heap, outside both the V8 sandbox cage and memory-protection keys. That means a bug there is not boxed in the way a V8 bug would be. Check Point found five bugs: two UAFs (node:zlib deflateParams and HTMLRewriter AttributesIterator), two URLPattern out-of-bounds reads, and a KV SQL authorizer bypass leading to arbitrary deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes into workerd's internal structured-clone deserializer.
- Cross-tenant secret theft via URLPattern OOB: a nested capture group like /(ab(cde))/ causes V8 to report two capture groups while nameList holds only one name. The loop reads 24 bytes past the vector end, treats them as a kj::String, and dereferences ptr, returning bytes at an attacker-chosen address. Using tcmalloc free-list layout and VFS file buffers as stable in-place primitives, one Worker can sweep the shared heap and read another tenant's secrets (Bearer tokens, private keys) without touching the cage or MPK-protected pages.

item.title: Don't Revoke That Token Yet: Inside the keyv/cacheable npm Worm, (Wed, Aug 5th)
item.description:
The keyv/cacheable npm worm flips incident response instinct on its head: revoking the stolen npm token does not neutralize the payload, it triggers it.
Key findings:
- The malicious package was designed so that token revocation is the activation condition, not a remediation step. Standard supply-chain IR muscle memory (revoke, rotate, cycle) is weaponized against the responder.
- Any build host that executed the compromised keyv or cacheable package should be treated as fully compromised. Scope your investigation to CI/CD pipeline nodes, not just developer workstations.
- DFIR priority shifts from credential hygiene to artifact preservation: capture memory, process trees, network connections, and filesystem changes before touching any credentials in the environment.
- The worm classification means lateral spread is possible across dependent packages or build environments. Map your dependency graph for keyv and cacheable consumers before containment.
Takeaway: Before revoking anything, image the affected build host and pull network logs. Establish the blast radius first. Token rotation comes after you understand what the payload does on activation, not before. Check the SANS ISC report for the full behavioral breakdown and IOC list.

item.title: The iOS 27 Recovery Menu: What It Means for Forensics
item.description:
iOS 27's new pre-boot recovery menu changes the seizure threat model for mobile examiners, not because it breaks encryption, but because it is three seconds from a factory wipe and auto-joins Wi-Fi before the data volume ever unlocks.
- The menu is reached by powering off, then holding the side button through boot. No cable required, no broken device required. Any healthy iPhone, any user, any time. It contains Erase All Content and Settings, Recovery Assistant (which erased at least one iPhone 11 in beta testing without warning), and Nearby Device Recovery, which can trigger a full restore from a helper phone.
- AFU state is destroyed the moment you enter this menu because it requires a full power cycle. BFU from that point forward. The oldest rule in mobile forensics applies unchanged: do not reboot the evidence.
- The recovery environment auto-joins known Wi-Fi with no credential and no user session. An isolated evidence device that recognizes a lab network can pull a firmware update and move to a version your tooling does not yet support. Faraday from seizure, and audit every network the device has seen.
- Diagnostics Mode will display serial number and IMEI on a locked, unpaired device with no pairing record. Useful for identification when the SIM tray is missing and the case is unreadable. Do not accept the config profile or transmit logs. Data leaving the device is a chain-of-custody event and may alert the account holder.

item.title: TP-Link Omada flaws could allow attackers to infiltrate industrial network infrastructure through zero-touch provisioning
item.description:
15 new flaws in TP-Link Omada's Zero-Touch Provisioning platform chain together to compromise controllers, cloud services, and managed devices across enterprise and industrial networks at scale.
Key findings:
- Hard-coded private keys and TLS certs are the backbone of the chain: CVE-2025-15627 embeds a hardcoded private key in Omada protocol v1, CVE-2025-15628 does the same for a v2 TLS cert, and that same root key signs firmware updates across Omada, Festa, Tapo, Kasa, and VIGI product lines. One key extraction enables MitM across 70+ million app installs.
- The attack chain runs from unauthenticated device adoption to root RCE. An external attacker enumerates sequential serial numbers (FSCT-2025-0011), races the cloud adoption handshake by spoofing a MAC (CVE-2025-15630), harvests credential hashes weakened by empty salts (CVE-2025-9290), then pivots to OS command injection as root via CVE-2025-7850.
- Credential exposure is systemic: site passwords transmit in cleartext (CVE-2025-15544), device passwords are stored as unsalted MD5 encrypted with a hard-coded key (CVE-2025-15631), and the RC4 key protecting v1 protocol traffic is predictable (CVE-2025-15629).
- VIGI surveillance and shared cloud accounts amplify blast radius. A compromised Omada cloud account can pivot into VIGI Cloud VMS, potentially exposing video feeds at critical facilities.

item.title: Weaponizing Windows Updates with NotWSUSpicious
item.description:
SpecterOps releases NotWSUSpicious, a tool that weaponizes enterprise WSUS servers configured with external MSSQL backends, turning the update pipeline into a payload delivery mechanism against any managed endpoint.
Key details:
- The attack requires WSUS to use an external MSSQL server with EPA disabled. PetitPotam coerces the WSUS computer account (WSUS1$) into authenticating to the attacker, ntlmrelayx relays that NTLM auth to MSSQL port 1433 via SOCKS, and a custom mssqlclient.py connects to the SUSDB database as the machine account (T1557.001, T1021.002).
- NotWSUSpicious.py generates the full SQL stored-procedure chain: spImportUpdate, spSaveXmlFragment, spSetBatchURL, spCreateTargetGroup, spAddComputerToTargetGroup, and spDeployUpdate. The tool calculates SHA1 and SHA256 hashes of the payload and injects them into WSUS update metadata so the file passes integrity checks.
- Payload delivery abuses BITS: a bundled BitsWebServer.py serves the malicious file over HTTP range requests, which WSUS fetches natively. The update appears legitimate to the target machine, which executes the payload at next check-in.
- Detection opportunities: anomalous MSSQL sessions authenticating as a computer account (WSUS1$) to the SUSDB database, unexpected rows in SUSDB update tables with attacker-controlled GUIDs, and BITS traffic (HTTP 206 responses) from non-Microsoft hosts serving update files.

item.title: Shai-Hulud strikes again: CHAINDROP worm hits 400+ npm packages
item.description:
CHAINDROP worm compromises 400+ npm packages via stolen credentials and preinstall hooks, targeting developer machines with a credential harvester capable of draining AI, cloud, and CI/CD secrets.

item.title: Turning Enterprise Update Servers Into Backdoor Factories (0_o) – Part 1
item.description:
WSUS NTLM relay technique weaponizes the upstream server's computer account to inject malicious updates directly into the SUSDB, enabling surgical payload delivery to individual targets without touching a domain controller.
- When WSUS uses an external MSSQL backend, coercing the upstream WSUS computer account (e.g., WSUS1$) via PetitPotam and relaying with Ntlmrelayx grants a MSSQL session as that machine account. The account lands in the webService database role, which carries EXECUTE on stored procedures but no direct table access, so the entire attack chain runs through stored procedures only.
- The attack chain calls six stored procedures in sequence: spImportUpdate (registers the malicious update with a custom UpdateXml payload), spSaveXmlFragment three times per update for UpdateIdentity, LocalizedProperties, and ExtendedProperties fragments, spSetBatchURL (points the file hash to an attacker-controlled download URL in tbFile), then spCreateTargetGroup and spAddComputerToTargetGroup to scope delivery to a single machine, and finally spDeployUpdate to approve and push the payload.
- Surgical targeting is the key threat: spGetComputerTargetByName returns a ComputerID, which lets the attacker add one specific host to a custom TargetGroup. Only that host receives the malicious update, limiting noise and evading broad detection.

item.title: Turning Enterprise Update Servers Into Backdoor Factories (0_o) – Part 2
item.description:
WSUS signature verification bypass lets attackers deploy unsigned payloads via enterprise update infrastructure, turning patch management into a persistence mechanism with no user interaction required.
- WSUS enforces digital signature checks on downloaded executables, but Microsoft.UpdateServices.ContentSyncAgent.dll (a .NET assembly in C:\Program Files\Update Services\Services) contains a VerifyFile function that skips CheckCertificateSignature entirely if the filename ends in .txt or .esd. Renaming a payload Ghost.txt is enough to pass verification and trigger a FileVerified log event instead of failure.
- The full attack chain: inject a malicious update via SQL stored procedures (spCreateTargetGroups, spSetBatchURL, spDeployUpdate), host the payload on a BITS-compatible web server supporting Range headers, and deliver it to targeted workgroups. If "Auto download and schedule install" group policy is enabled, zero user interaction is needed.
- WSUS logs at C:\Program Files\Update Services\LogFiles are the primary artifact. Watch for FileVerificationFailed events, then FileVerified events on .txt or .esd filenames. The payload process runs for a few hours then exits, but the update redeploys automatically, creating persistent C2 re-entry.
- The researcher released NotWSUSPicious to automate malicious update creation. Detection: alert on spSetBatchURL calls referencing .txt or .esd files, and spDeployUpdate executions from non-computer accounts.

item.title: From open lures to cloaked gates: How a macOS ClickFix campaign learned to hide
item.description:
A macOS ClickFix campaign distributing MacSync and AMOS infostealers evolved from openly serving malicious lures to hiding behind a server-side browser-fingerprinting gate, sharply reducing visibility for crawlers and sandboxes.
- Over 250 algorithmically named domains follow a recognizable pattern (file<word><word>[.]com, e.g. fileoceanhammer[.]sbs, filevelvettractor[.]sbs) serving a lightweight ~2.5 KB JS fingerprinting gate. The gate collects navigator, screen, WebGL GPU signals, timezone offset, iframe state, and touch support, then silently POSTs the fingerprint back with a mode:"php" tag. Only requests consistent with a real macOS desktop browser receive the ClickFix lure; crawlers and sandboxes get a blank or decoy page, making the infrastructure appear benign to automated analysis.
- The infection chain: qualifying visitors see a GitHub-themed "Verified Publisher / Download for macOS" page at domains like apricotfilepoint[.]com, copy an obfuscated curl one-liner to Terminal, which fetches a remote script from a /curl/<id> path, chains through multiple script stages, and ultimately drops and executes Atomic Stealer (AMOS), harvesting keychain items, browser credentials, crypto wallets, and SSH keys before exfiltrating via HTTP POST.

item.title: OT Security Analysis: Exposed Devices Attacked in US Water Systems
item.description:
Coordinated attacks hit 30+ water systems across 12 US 🇺🇸 states, targeting internet-exposed Rockwell Allen-Bradley PLCs via cellular connections, with confirmed logic modification and loss of operational control.
Key findings:
- Threat actors targeted MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 PLCs via EtherNet/IP (port 44818), an unauthenticated protocol that can allow remote config writes. At least one victim had PLC logic modified; others had IP addresses and passwords changed remotely, causing pressure loss and flooding risk. No attribution confirmed, though TTPs overlap with a concurrent CISA advisory on Iranian-affiliated actors targeting exposed PLCs.
- Forescout found 4,407 devices exposing port 44818 on Shodan as of August 3, 2026. 65% are in the US 🇺🇸, and over 70% of US-facing devices sit on mobile carrier networks, matching the cellular-connected attack surface described in the FBI/EPA advisory. 22 devices were identified in cities named in the campaign.

Notable unpatched CVEs include CVE-2016-5645 (hardcoded SNMP read-write strings) and CVE-2017-7899 (credentials in cleartext via HTTP GET). item.title: When Attackers Hijack Your Inbox: Detecting Mailbox Forwarding Rules with Microsoft Defender XDR
item.description:
BEC attackers silently hijack M365 mailboxes using forwarding rules. Five KQL hunting queries in Defender XDR Advanced Hunting expose the full post-compromise chain from suspicious sign-in to persistence.
- Mailbox forwarding rules (New-InboxRule and Set-Mailbox ActionTypes in CloudAppEvents) are a core BEC persistence technique (T1114.003). Attackers use three variants: "Forward to" rules, "Redirect to" rules (which preserve original sender, making exfiltration harder to spot), and direct mailbox forwarding via Set-Mailbox. All three are captured by Microsoft Purview Audit and available in Defender XDR Advanced Hunting in near real time.
- The correlation queries are where this gets powerful. Use Case 4 joins EntraIdSignInEvents with CloudAppEvents to flag a suspicious sign-in (geographic deviation, unmanaged device, missing user agent) followed by forwarding rule creation within 24 hours. Use Case 5 joins AlertEvidence with forwarding events to surface post-alert persistence within an 8-hour window, answering "what did the attacker do next."
- Additional detection logic covers: forwarding rules on high-value accounts (exec, finance, legal) via a user filter; three or more mailboxes forwarding to the same external address (bulk compromise signal); and rules forwarding to consumer domains like gmail[.]com, yahoo[.]com, outlook[.]com, and proton[.]me.

item.title: SMOKE#SCREEN Campaign Abuses ScreenConnect to Give Attackers Remote Control Access
item.description:

- The attacker pivoted mid-campaign from a 9-step Defender destruction sequence (disabling AMSI, killing WinDefend, adding C:\ as an exclusion, stripping Zone.Identifier) to a stealth loader containing a hardcoded 180-second sleep with a source comment explicitly stating it breaks Elastic EDR correlation windows.
